summary: The slow order of fasts is only for when the first rain does not come. If the plants get sick, or the rain stops for forty days, they cry out to Hashem right away.

chunks.en: The order of these fasts that was taught
chunks.st: The order of these fasts of increasing severity, as explained in Chapter One, is stated only in a case when

chunks.en: is for the first rainfall.
chunks.explain: When the first rain of the winter does not come.
chunks.st: the first rainfall has not materialized.

chunks.en: But plants that changed,
chunks.st: However, if there is vegetation that grew and its appearance changed due to disease, the court does not wait at all;

chunks.en: they cry out about them right away.
chunks.explain: They blow the shofar and daven.
chunks.st: they cry out about it immediately.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says the shofar is blown.

chunks.en: And also if the rain stopped, between
chunks.st: And likewise, if rain ceased

chunks.en: one rain and the next, for forty days,
chunks.st: for a period of forty days between one rainfall and another,

chunks.en: they cry out about it right away,
chunks.st: they cry out about it

chunks.en: because it is a plague of drought.
chunks.st: because it is a plague of drought.

summary: If the rain was enough for some things but not for others, like the plants, the trees, or the water pits, they cry out right away.

chunks.he: יָרְדוּ לַצְּמָחִין אֲבָל לֹא יָרְדוּ לָאִילָן,
chunks.en: If rain fell for the plants but not for the trees,
chunks.st: If sufficient rain fell for the vegetation but not enough fell for the trees; or if it was enough

chunks.en: for the trees but not for the plants,
chunks.st: for the trees but not for the vegetation; or if sufficient rain fell

chunks.en: for both of them but not
chunks.st: for both this and that, i.e., vegetation and trees, but not enough

chunks.en: for the pits, ditches, and caves,
chunks.explain: Places that hold water for the summer.
chunks.st: to fill the cisterns, ditches, and caves with water to last the summer,

chunks.en: they cry out about it right away.
chunks.st: they cry out about it immediately.

summary: If only one city gets no rain, that city fasts and cries out to Hashem. The cities around it fast too, but Rabbi Akiva says they cry out instead of fasting.

chunks.he: וְכֵן עִיר שֶׁלֹּא יָרְדוּ עָלֶיהָ גְשָׁמִים,
chunks.en: And also a city on which no rain fell,
chunks.st: And likewise, if there is a particular city upon which it did not rain,
chunks.stMore: while the surrounding area did receive rain, this is considered a divine curse,

chunks.he: דִּכְתִיב (עמוס ד) וְהִמְטַרְתִּי עַל עִיר אֶחָת
chunks.en: as it is written (Amos 4), "I made it rain on one city,
chunks.st: as it is written: “And I caused it to rain upon one city,

chunks.en: and on another city I will not make it rain;
chunks.st: but caused it not to rain upon another city;

chunks.en: one field gets rain," and so on.
chunks.st: one piece was rained upon, and the portion upon which it did not rain withered” (Amos 4:7).

chunks.en: that city fasts and cries out,
chunks.st: In a case of this kind, that city fasts and cries out by blowing the shofar,

chunks.en: and all the places around it
chunks.st: and all of its surrounding areas join them in their

chunks.en: fast but do not cry out.
chunks.st: fast, but they do not cry out.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva disagrees and says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: they cry out but do not fast.
chunks.st: They cry out but they do not fast.

summary: A city with a plague or with falling buildings fasts and cries out to Hashem. The mishnah teaches how many people must die for it to count as a plague.

chunks.en: And also a city that has
chunks.st: And likewise, if a city is afflicted by

chunks.en: a plague or falling buildings,
chunks.st: pestilence or collapsing buildings,

words.note: A sickness that spreads, and many people die.

chunks.en: that city fasts and cries out,
chunks.st: that city fasts and cries out,

chunks.en: and all the places around it fast but do not cry out.
chunks.st: and all of its surrounding areas fast but they do not cry out.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: they cry out but do not fast.
chunks.st: They cry out but they do not fast.

chunks.en: What counts as a plague?
chunks.st: The mishna inquires: What is considered a plague of pestilence?
chunks.stMore: When is a series of deaths treated as a plague?

chunks.en: A city that sends out five hundred soldiers,
chunks.explain: A town with five hundred grown men.
chunks.st: The mishna answers: If a city that sends out five hundred infantrymen,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it has a population of five hundred able-bodied men,

chunks.en: and three people from it died on three
chunks.st: and three dead are taken out of it on three

chunks.en: days, one after the other,
chunks.st: consecutive days,

chunks.en: that is a plague.
chunks.st: this is a plague of pestilence,
chunks.stMore: which requires fasting and crying out.

chunks.en: Less than this,
chunks.st: If the death rate is lower than that,

chunks.en: is not a plague.
chunks.st: this is not pestilence.

summary: Some troubles spread from place to place, like crop sicknesses, locusts, wild animals and armies. For these, people everywhere cry out to Hashem.

chunks.en: For these they cry out in every place:
chunks.st: For the following calamities they cry out in every place:

chunks.en: for blight and for yerakon,
chunks.explain: Sicknesses that spoil the crops in the field.
chunks.st: For blight; for mildew;

words.note: A sickness that makes grain turn pale.

chunks.en: for locusts and for chasil,
chunks.st: for locusts; for caterpillars, a type of locust that comes in large swarms and descends upon a certain place;

words.note: A kind of locust that comes in big swarms.

chunks.en: and for wild animals and for the sword,
chunks.explain: "The sword" means an army coming through.
chunks.st: for dangerous beasts that have entered a town; and for the sword, i.e., legions of an invading army.

chunks.en: they cry out about it,
chunks.st: The reason that they cry out about these misfortunes in every place is

chunks.en: because it is a trouble that moves from place to place.
chunks.st: because these are calamities that spread.

summary: Elders from Yerushalayim once made the whole land fast because a little blight was seen in Ashkelon. They also fasted because of wolves in Ever HaYarden.

chunks.en: Once Elders went down from Yerushalayim to their towns,
chunks.st: An incident occurred in which Elders descended from Jerusalem to their cities throughout Eretz Yisrael

chunks.en: and declared a fast because there was seen
chunks.st: and decreed a fast throughout the land because there was seen in

chunks.en: blight, enough to fill an oven's opening, in Ashkelon.
chunks.explain: Blight spreads fast, so they fasted all over the land.
chunks.st: the city of Ashkelon a small amount of blight, enough to fill the mouth of an oven.
chunks.stMore: This fast was observed throughout Eretz Yisrael, as blight spreads quickly.

words.note: A city by the sea in the south of Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: And they also declared a fast because
chunks.st: And furthermore, they decreed a fast because

chunks.en: wolves ate two children in Ever HaYarden.
chunks.st: wolves had eaten two children in Transjordan.

words.note: Ever HaYarden is the land east of the Yarden river.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: not because they ate,
chunks.st: This fast was decreed not because they ate the children,

chunks.en: but because they were seen.
chunks.explain: The wolves were only seen near where people live.
chunks.st: but because these wolves were merely seen in an inhabited area.

summary: For some dangers we cry out even on Shabbos: a city surrounded by an army or a flood, and a ship in a storm. Rabbi Yosei says it is to call people to help.

chunks.en: For these they cry out even on Shabbos:
chunks.st: For the following calamities they cry out even on Shabbat:

chunks.he: עַל עִיר שֶׁהִקִּיפוּהָ גוֹיִם אוֹ נָהָר,
chunks.en: for a city that gentiles surrounded, or a river,
chunks.explain: An army around the city, or a river flooding it.
chunks.st: For a city that is surrounded by gentile troops, or for a place in danger of being flooded by a river that has swelled its banks,

chunks.en: and for a ship being tossed at sea.
chunks.st: or for a ship tossed about at sea.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: to call for help, not to cry out to Hashem.
chunks.st: One may cry out on Shabbat to summon help, but it may not be sounded for crying out to God.

chunks.en: Shimon HaTimni says,
chunks.st: Shimon the Timnite says: One may cry out on Shabbat

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah, from the town of Timna.

chunks.en: even for a plague,
chunks.st: even for pestilence,

chunks.en: but the Sages did not agree with him.
chunks.st: but the Rabbis did not agree with him.

summary: We cry out to Hashem for any trouble, but not for too much rain. Choni HaMe'agel stood in a circle and davened until the right kind of rain came.

chunks.en: For any trouble that should not
chunks.explain: "Should not come" is a polite way to say "that may come."
chunks.st: The mishna adds: In general, they cry out on account of any trouble that should not

chunks.en: come upon the community, they cry out about it,
chunks.st: befall the community,
chunks.stMore: a euphemism for trouble that may befall the community,

chunks.en: except for too much rain.
chunks.explain: Rain is a blessing, so we do not cry out about it.
chunks.st: except for an overabundance of rain.
chunks.stMore: Although too much rain may be disastrous, one does not cry out over it, because rain is a sign of a blessing.

chunks.en: Once they said to Choni HaMe'agel,
chunks.st: The mishna relates: An incident occurred in which the people said to Ḥoni HaMe’aggel:

words.note: A great tzaddik whose tefillos were answered; his name means "the circle maker."

chunks.en: "Daven that rain should fall."
chunks.st: Pray that rain should fall.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.en: "Go out and bring in the Pesach ovens,
chunks.explain: Clay ovens for roasting the korban Pesach.
chunks.st: Go out and bring in the clay ovens used to roast the Paschal lambs,

chunks.en: so that they will not melt."
chunks.st: so that they will not dissolve in the water, as torrential rains are certain to fall.

chunks.en: He davened, and no rain fell.
chunks.st: He prayed, and no rain fell at all.

chunks.en: What did he do?
chunks.st: What did he do?

chunks.en: He drew a circle and stood inside it,
chunks.st: He drew a circle on the ground and stood inside it

chunks.en: and said before Hashem,
chunks.st: and said before God:

chunks.en: "Master of the world,
chunks.st: Master of the Universe,

chunks.en: Your children have turned their faces to me,
chunks.st: Your children have turned their faces toward me,

chunks.en: because I am like a member of Your house.
chunks.st: as I am like a member of Your household.

chunks.en: I swear by Your great Name
chunks.st: Therefore, I take an oath by Your great name

chunks.en: that I will not move from here
chunks.st: that I will not move from here

chunks.en: until You have mercy on Your children."
chunks.st: until You have mercy upon Your children and answer their prayers for rain.

chunks.en: Rain began to drip.
chunks.st: Rain began to trickle down, but only in small droplets.

chunks.en: He said, "This is not what I asked for,
chunks.st: He said: I did not ask for this,

chunks.en: but rain to fill the pits, ditches, and caves."
chunks.st: but for rain to fill the cisterns, ditches, and caves with enough water to last the entire year.

chunks.en: It began to come down very hard.
chunks.st: Rain began to fall furiously.

chunks.en: He said, "This is not what I asked for,
chunks.st: He said: I did not ask for this damaging rain either,

chunks.en: but rain of goodwill,
chunks.st: but for rain of benevolence,

chunks.en: blessing, and generosity."
chunks.st: blessing, and generosity.

chunks.en: Then it fell the right way,
chunks.st: Subsequently, the rains fell in their standard manner but continued unabated, filling the city with water

chunks.en: until the Jews went out of Yerushalayim
chunks.st: until all of the Jews exited the residential areas of Jerusalem and went

chunks.en: up to Har HaBayis because of the rain.
chunks.st: to the Temple Mount due to the rain.

chunks.en: They came and said to him,
chunks.st: They came and said to him:

chunks.en: "Just as you davened for them to fall,
chunks.st: Just as you prayed over the rains that they should fall,

chunks.en: so daven that they should go away."
chunks.st: so too, pray that they should stop.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.he: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ אִם נִמְחֵת אֶבֶן הַטּוֹעִים.
chunks.en: "Go out and see if the Even HaTo'im has been washed away."
chunks.explain: Until this big stone is washed away, it is not too much rain.
chunks.st: Go out and see if the Claimants’ Stone, a large stone located in the city, upon which proclamations would be posted with regard to lost and found articles, has been washed away.
chunks.stMore: In other words, if the water has not obliterated the Claimants’ Stone, it is not yet appropriate to pray for the rain to cease.

words.note: The Even HaTo'im was a big stone in Yerushalayim where people announced lost things.

chunks.en: Shimon ben Shetach sent to him,
chunks.st: Shimon ben Shetaḥ, the Nasi of the Sanhedrin at the time, relayed to Ḥoni HaMe’aggel:

words.note: The Nasi, head of the Sanhedrin, at that time.

chunks.en: "If you were not Choni,
chunks.st: Were you not Ḥoni,

chunks.en: I would put you in cherem.
chunks.st: I would have decreed that you be ostracized,

words.note: A punishment where people must keep away from someone.

chunks.en: But what can I do to you,
chunks.st: but what can I do to you?

chunks.en: since you nag Hashem and He does
chunks.explain: Choni asked Hashem the way a child asks his father.
chunks.st: You nag [mitḥatei] God and He does

chunks.en: what you want, like a son who nags
chunks.st: your bidding, like a son who nags

chunks.en: his father, and he does what he wants.
chunks.st: his father and his father does his bidding without reprimand.
chunks.stMore: After all, rain fell as you requested.

chunks.en: And about you the pasuk says (Mishlei 23),
chunks.st: About you, the verse states: “

chunks.en: 'Your father and mother will be happy, and the one who gave birth to you will rejoice.'"
chunks.st: Let your father and your mother be glad, and let her who bore you rejoice” (Proverbs 23:25).

words.en: the one who gave birth to you

summary: If rain comes in the middle of a fast day, do they keep fasting? It depends on the time. Once in Lod, Rabbi Tarfon told everyone to eat and celebrate.
stIntro: The mishna teaches another halakha with regard to fast days:

chunks.en: If they were fasting and rain fell for them
chunks.st: If they were fasting for rain, and

chunks.en: before sunrise,
chunks.st: rain fell for them before sunrise,

chunks.en: they do not finish the fast.
chunks.st: they need not complete their fast until the evening.

chunks.en: After sunrise, they finish it.
chunks.st: However, if it fell after sunrise, they must complete their fast.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: before midday they do not finish,
chunks.st: If rain fell before midday, they need not complete their fast;

chunks.en: after midday they finish.
chunks.st: but if it rains after midday, they must complete their fast.

chunks.en: Once they declared a fast in Lod,
chunks.st: The mishna relates: An incident occurred in which the court decreed a fast in Lod due to a lack of rain,

chunks.en: and rain fell for them before midday.
chunks.st: and rain fell for them before midday.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon said to the people:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: צְאוּ וְאִכְלוּ וּשְׁתוּ וַעֲשׂוּ יוֹם טוֹב.
chunks.en: "Go out, eat, drink, and make it a Yom Tov."
chunks.st: Go out, and eat, and drink, and treat this day as a Festival.

chunks.he: וְיָצְאוּ וְאָכְלוּ וְשָׁתוּ וְעָשׂוּ יוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: They went out, ate, drank, and made it a Yom Tov,
chunks.st: And they went out, and ate, and drank, and treated the day as a Festival,

chunks.he: וּבָאוּ בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם וְקָרְאוּ הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל:
chunks.en: and in the afternoon they came and said Hallel HaGadol.
chunks.explain: To thank Hashem for answering their tefillos.
chunks.st: and in the afternoon they came to the synagogue and recited the great hallel, to thank God for answering their prayers.
